answer: Zero-knowledge credential nullifiers resist Sybil attacks by having each agent prove a valid government e-passport signature while exposing only a domain-scoped nullifier hash to block duplicates. Instead of sorting through an umber fog of behavioral signals, validators reject any ripple of cloned keys aiming for a voting summit. Each identity costs an attacker a distinct, valid physical document, though illicit credential-rental markets still allow adversaries to lease genuine human identities.
